To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report a novel method of using carbon nanotubes to assist the growth of high quality free-standing GaN films by hydride vapour phase epitaxy.

we developed a novel approach to fabricate high-quality free-standing GaN substrate grown by hydride vapour phase epitaxy (HYPE) using carbon nanotube (CNT) as a mask to weaken the interface connection, release the compressive strain and block the propagation of dislocation, resulting in the self-separation of the GaN substrate.
the CSCNTs assisted self-separation method can be applied to grow high quality 2-inches FS-GaN substrate with low defect density and good optical properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel method for fabrication of free-standing GaAs and GaP substrates by hy-dride vapor phase epitaxial (HVPE) growth on a cross-stacked carbon nano-tubes (CSCNs) coated sapphire substrate.
the development of a novel approach to fabricate high-quality 2-inch FS-GaN substrates with the help of cross-stacked carbon nano-tubes.
the growth of GaN films on the CSCNTs coated sapphire by HVPE and the fabrication of high quality 2" free standing GaN substrates.

the CSCNTs assisted self-separation technique can effectively reduce the TD density and enhance the crystalline quality and thus is a promising method for large area and high-quality GaN substrates fabrication.

the cross-stacked carbon nano tubes (CSCNT) assisted self-separation technique is a promising method for fabricating large size free standing GaN substrate by hydride vapour phase epitaxy (HVP) technique.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CSCNTs are a promising template to fabricate high-quality GaN substrates with high yield and low cost.
CSCNTs can serve as a novel nanomask for GaN substrate growth and self-separation.
CSCNTs are used as masks for the first time in GaN growth and the resulting FS-GaN substrates are of high quality with the help of CSCNTs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we demonstrate the first freestanding Ga-N substrate grown on cross-stack carbon nanotube coated sapphire.
we have shown a new way to grow high-quality GaN films on a sapphire substrate.
the CSCNTs can act as a nanoscale mask to help weaken the interface connections, release the compressive stresses and block the propagation of TDs during the growth of FS-GaN.
